group_assessment.weighting: Two small human studies in adults with type 1 diabetes: a first-in-human 13C-BHB magnetic resonance spectroscopy tracer study (5 diabetes, 6 controls) and an open-label randomised 4-week MCT-versus-isocaloric diet pilot (8 per arm) with clamped hypoglycaemia, working-memory tasks and fMRI. The observation (higher memory accuracy and some regional BOLD differences in the MCT arm at plasma BHB below 0.5 mmol/L) is firm as reported for 16 people; the interpretation that ketones supported brain metabolism is the authors' inference, and the accuracy outcome shows a ceiling effect. Adults with insulin-treated diabetes and insulin-induced hypoglycaemia; not neonates, not encephalopathy, not WWOX.

entries.proposition: The tracer study had 11 participants (5 with type 1 diabetes, 6 controls) and the diet trial 16 (8 per arm).
entries.snippet: A total of 11 individuals were enrolled in the MRS study.

entries.proposition: The clamp used insulin with a variable 20% dextrose infusion to hold plasma glucose at 50 mg/dL (2.8 mmol/L).
entries.snippet: Participants received a primed (200 mU/kg) continuous (2 mU/kg/min) intravenous infusion of insulin together with a variable 20% dextrose infusion adjusted to achieve the target plasma glucose level of 50 mg/dL (2.8 mmol/L).
Because of the distinctive taste of MCT oil, participants were not blinded to diet assignment.
entries.anchor: Methods, MCT Diet Study Experimental Protocol

entries.proposition: The sample size was set to detect a 5% difference in working-memory accuracy with eight participants per group.
entries.snippet: a sample size of eight participants with T1DM per group was calculated to provide 85% power

entries.proposition: The results sentence reports plasma BHB steady-state during infusion with '(2.8 mmol/L)' in brackets, which is the glucose clamp target; Figure 1A plots plasma BHB near 0.6-0.7 mmol/L.
entries.snippet: reached similar steady-state levels (60–90 min) during BHB infusion under clamped hypoglycemia (2.8 mmol/L)

entries.proposition: The text reports a higher relative contribution of labelled BHB to brain oxidative metabolism in type 1 diabetes (17.3% versus 13.7%).
entries.snippet: the relative contribution of labeled BHB to total oxidative capacity was significantly higher in astrocytes and neurons of participants with T1DM

entries.proposition: Figure 1J, K shows both total TCA flux and absolute ketone oxidation lower in type 1 diabetes (p < 0.0001); the higher relative contribution in panel L arises because the TCA denominator fell more than ketone oxidation, not because absolute BHB oxidation rose.
entries.snippet: Visual attestation of Figure 1J-L: V_tca total about 1.07 (healthy) versus 0.72 (T1DM) micromol/g/min; V_kb total about 0.060 versus 0.049; V_kb/V_tca total about 13.7% versus 17.3%; plasma BHB (panel A) about 0.6-0.7 mmol/L in both groups at steady state.

experimental_context.system: humans, 5 with type 1 diabetes and 6 healthy, 13C-MRS during insulin-hypoglycaemic clamp with BHB infusion
experimental_context.endpoint: modelled TCA and ketone oxidation rates

entries.qualifies_needle: the relative contribution of labeled BHB to total oxidative capacity was significantly higher

entries.proposition: On the primary memory outcome the MCT group had 100% accuracy and the ISO group 93% on the Sternberg digit tasks, with no reaction-time difference.
Figure 2C shows 6 of 8 MCT participants at 100% accuracy (ceiling), one at about 72%, the ISO group at 83-94%, and healthy controls median about 93% with a wide range.
entries.snippet: Visual attestation of Figure 2C, D: S6D accuracy; T1DM-MCT six of eight points at 100%, one near 94%, one near 72%; T1DM-ISO between about 83% and 94%; healthy median about 93%, range about 53-100%; p = 0.02 MCT versus ISO, p = 0.03 versus healthy; reaction time p = 0.31 and 0.23.

experimental_context.system: adults with type 1 diabetes after 4 weeks of MCT or isocaloric diet, and healthy controls, clamped hypoglycaemia

entries.proposition: The authors state plasma BHB stayed below 0.5 mmol/L in all participants with diabetes after four weeks of MCT.
entries.snippet: in fact, plasma BHB levels remained lower than 0.5 mmol/L in all participants with T1DM after the 4-week MCT-enriched diet

entries.proposition: Figure 3A shows BHB about 0.27 mmol/L before the clamp in the MCT group falling to about 0.13 at the memory test, against about 0.05-0.08 in the ISO group.
entries.snippet: Visual attestation of Figure 3A, B, C, E: BHB MCT about 0.27 at -20 min, 0.26 at 0, 0.13 at 65 and 100 min versus ISO about 0.07-0.05 mmol/L; FFA MCT about 0.43-0.49 then 0.16-0.15 versus ISO about 0.12-0.2; BHB AUC versus S6D accuracy r = 0.64, p = 0.01 pooling both diet groups; FFA AUC versus accuracy r = 0.37, p = 0.16.

experimental_context.system: adults with type 1 diabetes, diet groups pooled for correlations
experimental_context.endpoint: BHB and FFA concentrations and correlation with accuracy

entries.proposition: The Results state that both BHB and FFA AUCs strongly correlated with working memory performance; Figure 3E shows the FFA-accuracy correlation as not significant.
entries.snippet: strongly correlated with working memory performance measured by the S6D test
entries.anchor: Results, Association Between Circulating BHB and FFA Levels

entries.proposition: The Discussion says the brain-activity correlation is in the MCT group; the Figure 5 caption and axes show all participants pooled (n about 32).
entries.snippet: which showed a strong correlation between changes in regional brain activity and memory performance in the T1DMMCT group (Fig. 5)

entries.proposition: Figure 5 pools all three groups (about 32 points) for the BOLD-accuracy correlations (r 0.48, 0.48, 0.57); the MCT points are a subset.
entries.snippet: Visual attestation of Figure 5A-C: S6D accuracy against BOLD signal change with healthy (circles), ISO (open squares) and MCT (filled squares) points in one regression; L APC r = 0.48, L POIFG r = 0.48, DVACC r = 0.57.

experimental_context.system: all participants, three groups pooled, clamped hypoglycaemia fMRI

entries.proposition: The MCT diet modestly and non-significantly lowered epinephrine in n = 8 per group.
entries.snippet: The MCT diet produced a modest, nonsignificant decrease in plasma epinephrine during insulin-induced hypoglycemia

entries.proposition: The authors list small size, no baseline cognition and open-label design among limitations.
entries.snippet: Limitations included the small sample size impeding adjustment for potentially cognition-relevant covariates, limited cognitive domain testing with no baseline assessment, and incomplete continuous glucose monitoring data availability.

entries.proposition: The conclusion proposes the strategy may allow tighter glycaemic control without increased risk of hypoglycaemic brain injury.
entries.snippet: This novel nutritional strategy may allow tighter glycemic control in this vulnerable population without increasing the risk of hypoglycemia-induced brain injury.
